_doc: Family matters: consent to a match (blessing = your own parent, hand = the other person's parent or guardian, lord = the lord's leave for the unfree), apprenticeship, arranged matches. 'ask' lines are YOURS. Vars: {third} (the person in question) {thirdfull} {trade} {money} {ward} {names} {first1}.

ask: {Addr}, I wish to marry {third}. Will you give me your blessing?
I've found someone, {addr}. {Third}. I'd like your blessing.
{Third} and I want to wed. Will you stand with us?
It's {third}, {addr}. I'd like to ask your leave.

yes.t: You have it, {first}, and gladly. {Third} is a good match.
I'd hoped you would choose well. Go, and God bless you both.
Then it's settled. I'll speak to the priest myself.
My blessing, and my purse as far as it reaches.
I'd have chosen differently, perhaps. But I'm not the one marrying. Go.
I'd have chosen no differently myself.
God give you joy, {first}.

no.t: I cannot, {first}. {Third} is not what I'd want for you.
No. Not this match. I will not give leave.
Think again. I'd sooner see you wait than marry wrong.
I forbid it. The family's good name is not for spending.
Not this one. Find another.
I'll not give my blessing. Ask me again in a year if you still wish.

later.t: I'll need time to think on it, {first}. Ask again soon.
Give me some days. A match is not decided in a breath.
Come back in a few days. I must think on it.
Let me talk it over with the household first. Come back soon.

ask: {Addr}, I would ask for {third}'s hand in marriage.
With your leave, {addr}, I wish to wed {third}.
I come to ask you for {third}. I mean to do right by them.
{Third} and I are of one mind. Will you consent?

yes.t: I will, and gladly. You've shown yourself honest, {first}.
Then you have my leave. Treat {third} well.
A fine match, by my reckoning. Take my hand on it.
Aye. There's no one I'd sooner see my {third} with.
You may have my blessing. Be good to {third}.
I give {third} gladly.

no.t: No. I have other plans for {third}.
You are not what I'd want for them. I'm sorry.
Not a chance, {first}. You've not the means, nor the name.
I'll not hear it. Leave us.
Not while I draw breath.
Find a wife — a husband — elsewhere.

later.t: Let me think, {first}. This is no light thing.
Come again in a few days. I must speak with {third} first.
Come back in a few days. I must think on it.
Let me talk it over with the household first. Come back soon.

ask: My lord, I ask your leave to marry {third}.
I beg your permission to wed {third}, {addr}.
{Third} and I wish to marry. We ask your leave, and will pay the merchet.
With your leave, {addr}: I wish to take {third} to wife.

yes.t: You have it. The steward will name the fee. Merchet, as custom has it.
Granted. A marriage under my roof is no ill thing.
Granted, and may it be fruitful. The reeve will record it.
Aye, leave given. The merchet is due before Michaelmas.
Leave is given. Mark the merchet.
Be wed in God's name, and keep the peace of my manor.

no.t: Denied. I'll not lose a good pair of hands to another manor.
Not this one. Choose another within my lands.
You presume. Begone.
I cannot spare you from my lands.
Not this match. Choose another.

later.t: I will consider it. Ask me again when I am less pressed.
The steward must look at the roll of tenants. Wait.
Come back in a few days. I must think on it.
Let me talk it over with the household first. Come back soon.

ask: I'd like to learn a trade, {addr}. Could I be apprenticed to {third}, the {trade}?
I've watched {third} at the {trade}'s work. I'd like to be bound to them.
Will you send me to {third} to learn the {trade}'s craft?
I want to be more than a labourer. Would you pay for me to learn from {third}?

yes.t: A trade will serve you better than I ever could. Yes. It costs {money}, but you're worth it.
Very well. I'll speak to {third} and pay the {money}. Don't shame us.
Seven years is long, but a trade is for life. You go.
I'd hoped you'd choose. Work hard.
Then it's agreed. The indenture is for seven years.
I'll pay the {money}. Make it worth it.

no.t: {Third} won't have you, or I can't persuade them. Not this time.
No, {first}. The house needs you more than the craft does.
A trade? At your age? Hmph. Not yet.
The craft is not for us.
They have no room.

poor.t: We haven't the {money}, {first}. I'm sorry. Perhaps next year.
The premium is {money}. We cannot spare it.

ask: Would you speak for me to {thirdfull}'s family, {addr}? I'd like to be matched.
I'd like to marry {third}. Could you arrange it for me?
{Third} would suit me, {addr}. Might you open the talks?
Will you find me a match, {addr}? {Third}, perhaps?

yes.t: It's done. I've spoken to their people, and they're willing.
I'll see to it. A good match is half the battle, and this is a good match.
They agreed. The rest is for the priest and the neighbours.
They agree. We will see you wed.
It's arranged, {first}.

no.t: They were not interested, {first}. I tried.
They'd not hear of it. We might find a better.
They declined.
Let's look elsewhere.

dowry.t: They want about {money} with you. We haven't it just now.
A dowry of {money} is expected. Without it, the answer is no.

ask: I come with a proposal, {addr}: a match between my {ward} and your {third}.
I'd like our two houses joined: {ward} and {third}.
What would you think of {ward} and {third} together?
Our families are good neighbours. Might they be better? {Ward} and {third}.

yes.t: I think well of it. I accept.
You have my consent. Our houses are the stronger for it.
A fine match, and my {third} has said as much. Agreed.
Done. Come, we'll drink to it.
A good match. Agreed.
Our houses will be one.

no.t: No. I thank you for the offer, but I'll look elsewhere.
I cannot see it. Another time, perhaps.
My {third} deserves a better match than that.
We must decline.
Another time, perhaps.

dowry.t: A match, perhaps, but with a dowry of about {money}. Less, and I'll not hear it.
The terms are the thing. Bring {money}, and we'll talk.

ask: Whom do you think I might marry?
I've been thinking of settling down. Who would suit me?
Help me think, {addr}. Who is there?
You know the families hereabouts. Who might I court?
Who might suit me, do you think?
Whom would you advise me to marry?

reply.t: Let me think... {Names}. Any of them might suit.
I'd look at {first1} first, if I were you. Then there's {names}.
Good prospects: {names}. Courting takes time, so start soon.
{Names}. And I'll say this: choose with your head as much as your heart.

none.t: Slim pickings, {first}. Ask me when the harvest is in.
Nobody I'd put forward. Not yet.
Nobody comes to mind just now, {first}.

ask.t: Might I be fostered in {third}'s household, {addr}? I'd learn a lord's ways.
Will you send me to {third}? I should like to be trained in a great house.
A place in {third}'s household would do me good, {addr}. Will you ask for me?
I'm old enough to be bred up properly. {Third} keeps a fine house; let me go there.

yes.t: It is arranged. You will go to {third}'s household and learn what we cannot teach you.
A good house, a good name. Go, and do us credit.
{Third} has agreed. Mind your manners, mind your elders, and write home.

no.t: {Third} has no room. Not this year.
I'd miss you too much, child. Not yet.
The answer is no. We shall find another way.
